rules.title: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2
rules.requirement: An owner must have just cause to terminate a tenancy and provide a statement of cause in any notice to terminate after tenants have lawfully occupied the property for 12 months or more. For no-fault just cause terminations, the owner must provide relocation assistance equal to one month's rent or waive the final month's rent.
rules.key_value: relocation assistance equal to 1 month's rent or rent waiver
rules.summary_plain: Your landlord must have a valid reason to end your tenancy and must tell you why if you've lived there for a year or more. If they end your tenancy without fault, they must help you move by paying you one month's rent or letting you skip the last month's rent.
rules.summary_plain_es: Su arrendador debe tener una razón válida para terminar su contrato y debe decirle por qué si ha vivido allí un año o más. Si terminan su contrato sin culpa, deben ayudarle a mudarse pagando un mes de renta o dejándole no pagar el último mes.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to residential real property except certain exempt properties such as single-family owner-occupied residences with no more than two units, housing built within last 15 years (except mobilehomes), affordable housing, and others as specified.

conditions.note: Housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years is exempt unless a mobilehome
Single-family owner-occupied residences with no more than two units or bedrooms are exempt

rules.exemptions_text: Exemptions include transient and tourist hotel occupancy, nonprofit hospital and religious facility housing, dormitories, owner-occupied single-family residences with up to two units, housing built within last 15 years (except mobilehomes), affordable housing, and others as detailed in the statute.
rules.penalty: Owner who violates this section is liable for actual damages, reasonable attorney's fees and costs, and up to three times actual damages plus punitive damages if willful or malicious.
rules.quoted_span: (c) Before an owner of residential real property issues a notice to terminate a tenancy for just cause that is a curable lease violation, the owner shall first give notice of the violation to the tenant with an opportunity to cure the violation pursuant to paragraph (3) of Section 1161 of the Code of Civil Procedure... (d)(1) For a tenancy for which just cause is required to terminate the tenancy under subdivision (a), if an owner of residential real property issues a termination notice based on a no-fault just cause described in paragraph (2) of subdivision (b), the owner shall, regardless of the tenant’s income, at the owner’s option, do one of the following: (A) Assist the tenant to relocate by providing a direct payment to the tenant as described in paragraph (3). (B) Waive in writing the payment of rent for the final month of the tenancy, prior to the rent becoming due.
rules.preempts_note: Local ordinances requiring just cause adopted before or after September 1, 2019, that are more protective than this section apply instead of this state law.
